items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby child protection review finds departmental failings
items.description: Nearly three months since the death of Kumanjayi Little Baby, a review into her family circumstances prior to the tragedy has been handed down.

items.title: Private firms profit as Australia's job system fails workers, report finds
items.description: A new report argues Australia's employment services system is failing jobseekers, while filling the pockets private equity and millionaires.

items.title: Live: Hanson says she 'never advocated for the White Australia policy'
items.description: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has said she was not advocating for the White Australia policy when referencing it in an interview with far-right podcaster Tommy Robinson last week. Follow live.

items.title: Anthony Albanese on the night in parliament he would rather not relive
items.description: From left-wing roots to "radical centre" prime minister, Anthony Albanese reflects on his 30-year career in Parliament House.

items.title: Live: Board member of firebombed synagogue gives emotional evidence
items.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion is this week focused on security for the Australian Jewish community.

items.title: 'Happening to everybody': AI-manipulated images exploited by scammers
items.description: Papua New Guinea prepares new laws to criminalise the malicious use of artificial intelligence, including deepfakes, voice cloning and digital impersonation.

items.title: Women with hormone condition may face higher risk of heart attack, stroke
items.description: Women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS formerly PCOS) have a "significantly higher" risk of cardiovascular disease than those without, a new study suggests.

items.title: Australian EV owners deal with 'range anxiety'. China has almost eliminated it
items.description: You can swap an empty electric vehicle battery in about four minutes in China. It is part of how China has come to dominate the EV industry.

items.title: Six years out from hosting the Olympics, this is where Brisbane stands
items.description: Broken promises and scarcely broken ground. Five years since Brisbane secured the 2032 Olympic Games, this is the state of play.

items.title: US to impose 50pc tariffs on most Canadian goods
items.description: The White House says the tariffs will go into effect in 30 days, meaning there is time for negotiations.

items.title: Live: ASX falls as oil prices near one-month high on US-Iran escalation
items.description: The Australian share market has fallen after a negative session on Wall Street. Oil prices remain near a one-month high as Yemen's Houthis threaten to impose a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia. See how the trading day unfolds on our blog. Follow live.

items.title: US launches new strikes as Trump says Iran will 'pay' for soldiers' deaths
items.description: The United States has launched a new wave of strikes on Iran after identifying two soldiers killed while defending against Iranian missile and drone attacks in Jordan.

items.title: Iran-backed Houthis declare maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia
items.description: In a statement, the Houthis' military spokesperson Yahya Saree says the group will enforce the blockade against its "criminal Saudi enemy", effective immediately.

items.title: Quiz: How well do you remember these Australian kids' TV shows?
items.description: What was the name of the tough, mangy cat in The Ferals? And which show featured EC, the faceless doll?

items.title: Why 'narcissist' bosses are more likely to oppose work from home
items.description: Research published last month found narcissistic leaders — those with a tendency to be self-centred and entitled — were more likely than others to resist remote work. Why? The study concluded "it interferes with their motivations for power and status".

items.title: The discipline behind royal wedding cellist's success
items.description: Sheku Kanneh-Mason went viral performing at Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's wedding. He's captivated audiences since and is touring Australia this month.

items.title: 'Sit down!' Joyce's dog interrupts 7.30 interview as he defends Hanson
items.description: The One Nation MP says Pauline Hanson's meeting with far-right British activist Tommy Robinson did not amount to an endorsement of his criminal conduct, rejecting suggestions she had crossed a "red line". The otherwise serious 7.30 interview was twice interrupted by Mr Joyce's dog, prompting him to yell at it to "sit down".

items.title: Prepare for stock market pain as China throws a spanner into AI boom
items.description: Elon Musk's latest venture sent global stock markets to dizzying heights, but its performance since does not augur well for the company or the future of the AI boom.

items.title: Whistleblower's fight to unmask one of WA's worst child abusers
items.description: Maggie Dawkins's efforts to shine a light on the horrific abuses committed by Dennis McKenna against a generation of boys in Katanning are set down in a new book.

items.title: The four sets of data that show how the property market is transforming
items.description: Global instability, shifting tax policies and interest rate pressures force buyers and sellers to adjust to the changing property landscape.

items.title: Broncos winger Josiah Karapani handed $350 fine for drink-driving offence
items.description: Brisbane Broncos winger Josiah Karapani avoids a criminal conviction after pleading guilty to a drink-driving offence.

items.title: Firewood side hustle sparks multi-million-dollar business in four states
items.description: When bushfire and drought robbed farmer Peter Chauncy of his livelihood, he started chopping wood to sell. Forty years later, he runs one of Australia's largest firewood businesses.

items.title: Person found dead, child injured in Perth's south-east
items.description: Two crime scenes are established in Perth's south-east after a body is discovered and a teenage girl is found injured in a neighbouring suburb.

items.title: Union boss accused of 'bullying' by Fire Rescue Victoria commissioner
items.description: Victoria's fire rescue commissioner has written a strongly worded letter to the secretary of the United Firefighters Union, accusing him of aggressive and inappropriate communication amid a long-running conflict.

items.title: Tiny 'desert' fish found only in Australia narrowly avoids extinction
items.description: With scoops made from milk bottles, volunteers have been working tirelessly to save the red-fin blue-eye, found nowhere else in the world, from extinction.
